reason: csrf_meta_tags: Rails renders csrf-param/csrf-token meta tags nothing reads (Inertia sends the XSRF-TOKEN cookie as X-XSRF-TOKEN in both kits); this kit keeps its CSRF secret out of the HTML.
Loco's mailer always sends multipart/alternative (text + html); the Rails kit sends html only. The HTML part is identical, the text part carries the same copy and link.

Rails sends the string "Password challenge is invalid"; its own delete-user.tsx calls .map on it and the page crashes (TypeError, blank page, reproduced in Chromium). This kit sends ["Password challenge is invalid"], the shape the frontend expects.

Security: with password_challenge: null Rails skips the challenge (with_defaults fills only a missing key; has_secure_password validates a non-nil challenge) and changes the email without the password. This kit rejects it as "is invalid".
DENY instead of Rails' SAMEORIGIN, matching the CSP's frame-ancestors 'none': the kit's pages are never framed.
No ETag on dynamic pages: they carry per-request CSRF cookies and are private, must-revalidate; Rack::ETag only saves bandwidth after rendering the whole page anyway.
`accept-encoding` is added by the app's own compression layer (the Rails image compresses in Thruster, in front of Rails, so the app's responses don't vary).
The security headers go on every response, including public files and 404s (Rails' static file server and exceptions app skip them). Stricter, never weaker.
A 404 is `no-cache` so a CDN never caches a missing asset as if it existed; charset spelled `utf-8` (Rails' PublicExceptions writes `UTF-8`, the same charset).
robots.txt, icons and error pages aren't fingerprinted: one hour instead of one year, so a changed icon reaches returning visitors. Fingerprinted /vite/* assets are immutable for a year in both kits.

Security: no account enumeration. Rails answers unknown/unverified emails with an alert on the reset form and verified ones with a notice on sign-in, which reveals whether a verified account exists. This kit gives every request the same reply (redirect to sign-in with one neutral notice); only verified accounts get the mail.

Security: verification links are single-use. Rails binds the token to the email only, so a used link keeps 'verifying' until it expires; here verify only succeeds while the user is unverified, so a reused link is 'invalid'.
Organizations (docs/PARITY.md#organizations-a-deliberate-addition): every signed-in page carries the account switcher, the shared once prop `accounts` [{name, slug}].

match: ^(POST /sign_up (valid \(normalized email\)|bob)|POST /sign_in (second browser|right \(unnormalized email\)|with reset password|\(signed in\))|GET /sign_(in|up) \(signed in\)|GET / \(signed in\)|GET /dashboard|GET /dashboard \(html\)|POST /identity/email_verification \(resend, no referer\)) :: ?\.(status|location|head|page\.(url|component|deferredProps|props\.(account|membership)))$
reason: Organizations: sign-in, sign-up, `/` and `/dashboard` land on the user's account overview `/{account_slug}` (component accounts/show, deferred members_count) instead of the Rails kit's dashboard or home page. Same flash texts and mail.

Organizations: `/nope` has the shape of an account slug, so it matches `/{account_slug}` and a guest is sent to sign in (302), as on any signed-in page; a signed-in non-member gets the 404 page. Unknown paths that can't be a slug (`/robots.txt`, `/a`, two segments) still 404 as in Rails.

Asset tags: with the account pages in the build, Rolldown splits frontend/lib/browser.ts (one line, `isBrowser`) into its own 39-byte chunk that the entry imports, so the entry has one more `modulepreload` link. Same stylesheet and entry script; nothing else in the head changes.

Branding: the default app name (settings.app_name, the <title>) is "Inertia Rust Starter Kit" instead of the Rails kit's "React Starter Kit". bin/rename replaces it. The application-name meta tag carries the same name; it sits in head[1], already allowed above.

Branding: the kit's own favicon (an orange gear with two purple motion bars on a dark tile, the 16 px-safe version of frontend/components/app-logo-icon.tsx) instead of the Rails kit's red circle. Same paths, types and caching.
